mainTopic: The night before יום הכיפורים: the כהן גדול's oath against the צדוקים, interruptions during קריאת שמע, and keeping the כהן גדול awake
overview: This amud covers what happened the night before יום הכיפורים. First, the גמרא explains that the elders' oath to the כהן גדול binds him to the court's understanding of the עבודה. It does not make him their שליח. Then it explains why both sides cry. The oath was needed because the צדוקים lit the קטורת outside the קודש הקדשים, and a ברייתא tells of a צדוקי כהן גדול who did this and was punished from Heaven. A short story about pronouncing the name of רבי זכריה בן קבוטל leads to a discussion of interrupting קריאת שמע. That discussion brings in the readings of 'ודברת בם' and the ban on idle talk. A new משנה then describes how the young כהנים kept the כהן גדול awake: snapping their fingers, asking him to show קידה, and singing פסוקים. The amud ends with the custom of staying awake all night outside ירושלים, which led to sin in נהרדעא. אליהו's report about it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Can an agent do what the sender cannot?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's wording, where the elders call the כהן גדול their שליח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there anything that we cannot do ourselves, but our agents can do for us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that the כהן גדול is the שליח of the elders. Regular Jews cannot do the עבודה, so how could he be doing it on their behalf?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שליח can only do what his sender could legally do. A ישראל may not perform the עבודה in the קודש הקדשים. So calling the כהן גדול 'our שליח' seems to contradict the rules of שליחות.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there anything? (a question that expects the answer 'no')

steps.confusionAlert: This question is built on the principle that a שליח can only do what his sender can do. Because ישראלים cannot do the עבודה, the כהנים cannot be their agents. They are שלוחי דרחמנא, agents of Heaven. That is exactly why the elders' phrase 'our שליח' looks wrong.

phrases.english: Is there anything
that we are unable to do,
and our agents are able to do?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אִיכָּא מִידֵּי דַּאֲנַן לָא מָצֵינַן לְמֶעְבַּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of the משנה's oath wording earlier.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's phrase calling the כהן גדול the elders' שליח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A שליח cannot do what the sender cannot do. The elders cannot do the עבודה, so the כהן גדול cannot be their שליח for it.

steps.title: The oath means: follow the court's understanding
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reinterprets the wording. The oath binds him to the court's intent, not to an agency relationship.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what they were really saying to him: We make you swear according to our understanding and the understanding of the court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the elders were not making a claim about שליחות. They were making him swear according to their meaning, so he could not twist the oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of the wording is to block a loophole. He cannot say he swore with his own private meaning in mind. The question about agency disappears, because the משנה was never really talking about agency.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what they are saying to him (it reinterprets the words)
we make [you] swear / we administer an oath

steps.whyThisMatters: An oath taken 'על דעת' others cannot be escaped through hidden private meanings. This idea appears in other places in שבועות and נדרים.

phrases.english: This is what they say to him:
We make you swear

phrases.aramaic: עַל דַּעְתֵּינוּ וְעַל דַּעַת בֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: according to our understanding and the understanding of the court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The elders were declaring that the כהן גדול is their agent.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words only bind the oath to the court's understanding, so he cannot use private meanings to escape it.

steps.title: Why the כהן גדול cries
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and explains that the כהן גדול cries because he was suspected of being a צדוקי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'He turns aside and cries, and they turn aside and cry.' He cries because they suspected him of being a צדוקי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה. It explains why the כהן גדול cries: he is hurt that they suspected him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oath itself implied that he might secretly follow the צדוקים. Being suspected like this is a painful insult to an honest כהן גדול.

keyTerms.meaning: a Sadducee (a group that rejected the חכמים' tradition)

phrases.english: He turns aside and cries
and they turn aside and cry, etc.
He turns aside and cries —
phrases.notes: The גמרא now explains the quoted words.

phrases.english: because they suspected him of being a Sadducee,

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא פּוֹרֵשׁ וּבוֹכֶה וְהֵן פּוֹרְשִׁין וּבוֹכִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול cries out of hurt at being suspected of being a צדוקי.

steps.title: Why the elders cry
steps.stepSummary: The elders cry because, according to רבי יהושע בן לוי, whoever suspects innocent people is punished in his body.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they turn aside and cry, because רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Anyone who suspects proper people is stricken in his body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the elders also cry. It brings a teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כהן גדול is actually innocent, the elders have wrongly suspected him. That would make them deserve punishment. They had to make him swear, but they fear the cost of the suspicion.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known מוסר principle: wrongly suspecting others is a real sin. That is true even when the suspicion comes from a good reason.

phrases.english: and they turn aside and cry —
as Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Anyone who suspects proper people
is stricken in his body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of the משנה line begun in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever suspects innocent people is punished in his body. So the elders cry over their possibly false suspicion.

steps.title: Why was the oath needed at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the elders insisted so strongly on an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why all this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why such a dramatic oath was needed. This is a setup line, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making someone swear, and suspecting him, has a real cost, as we just saw. So the גמרא wants to know what danger made it worth it.

phrases.english: And why all this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the purpose of the oath, which caused all the crying.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What danger justified making the כהן גדול take an oath?

steps.title: To stop the צדוקים' way of offering the קטורת
steps.stepSummary: The oath ensures he will not light the קטורת outside and carry it in already burning, as the צדוקים did.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that he does not prepare the incense outside and then bring it in, the way the צדוקים do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the oath is meant to stop the כהן גדול from following the צדוקים' practice with the קטורת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the הלכה, the קטורת is placed on the coals only inside the קודש הקדשים. The צדוקים put it on outside and carried it in already smoking. Since he is alone inside and nobody can check, only an oath can make sure he does it correctly.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole oath exists because of the dispute with the צדוקים. The question is whether the קטורת is placed on the coals inside the קודש הקדשים (the הלכה) or outside before entering (the צדוקים).

phrases.english: So that he not prepare outside and bring in,
the way the Sadducees do.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The oath prevents the צדוקי practice of lighting the קטורת outside and carrying it into the קודש הקדשים.

steps.title: A צדוקי כהן גדול who actually did it
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells of a צדוקי כהן גדול who prepared the קטורת outside and came out very happy.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: There was a story with one צדוקי who prepared the incense outside and then brought it in. When he came out, he was extremely happy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story showing that the danger was real. A צדוקי כהן גדול really did offer the קטורת his way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story proves that the fear behind the oath was not just theory. The man's great joy shows that he did it on purpose and was proud of it.

phrases.english: Our Rabbis taught:
There was an incident with one Sadducee
who prepared outside and brought in.
When he came out, he was overjoyed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows with a real event that the danger described in step 6 actually happened.
steps.raayaObject: That a צדוקי כהן גדול really would prepare the קטורת outside.

steps.title: The father's warning
steps.stepSummary: His father warns him that even the צדוקים fear the פרושים and do not do this in practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: His father met him and said to him: My son, even though we are צדוקים, we are afraid of the פרושים.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. The צדוקי's own father is worried about what his son did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father admits that the צדוקים usually did not dare to act on their view. They were afraid of the פרושים. This shows how bold and unusual the son's act was.

phrases.english: His father met him,
and said to him: My son,
even though we are Sadducees,
we are afraid of the Pharisees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even the צדוקים normally avoided this practice out of fear of the פרושים.

steps.title: The son defends himself with a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The son answers that he had long wanted to fulfill the פסוק 'כי בענן אראה על הכפורת' according to the צדוקי reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: All my life I was troubled by this פסוק: 'For in the cloud I will appear over the כפורת.' I said: When will I get the chance to fulfill it? Now that I have the chance, should I not fulfill it?!
steps.whatsHappening: The son explains that he acted out of belief in the צדוקי reading of the פסוק. He waited his whole life for the chance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The צדוקים read the פסוק to mean that the cloud of קטורת must already be there when the כהן enters. That is why they lit it outside. The חכמים read it differently, so the son's act broke the הלכה. The story continues next.

keyTerms.meaning: in the cloud I will appear

steps.confusionAlert: The son's reading of 'בענן אראה' is the צדוקי reading, not the הלכה. Do not take his argument as the גמרא's own view.

phrases.english: He said to him:
All my days I was troubled
over this verse:
"For in the cloud I will appear over the Ark cover,"
I said: When will it come into my hands so that I can fulfill it?
Now that it has come into my hands —
shall I not fulfill it?!

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל יָמַי הָיִיתִי מִצְטַעֵר עַל הַמִּקְרָא הַזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The son answers his father's warning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The צדוקי based his practice on reading 'כי בענן אראה על הכפורת' to mean the cloud must already be there when he enters.

steps.title: The צדוקי כהן גדול dies a shameful death
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים report that within a few days the צדוקי כהן גדול died, was thrown on a garbage heap, and worms came out of his nose.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: only a few days passed before he died and was thrown onto the garbage dump, and worms were coming out of his nose.
steps.whatsHappening: The story of the צדוקי כהן גדול ends with his punishment. He died within days and his body was disgraced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the first version of his punishment. He died a few days after יום כיפור, not right away. His body was disgraced, thrown on a garbage dump with worms coming out of his nose.

phrases.english: They said: not even a few days passed
until he died and was thrown on the garbage dump,
and worms were coming out of his nose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story of the צדוקי כהן גדול by describing his punishment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The צדוקי כהן גדול died within a few days, in disgrace.

steps.title: A second version: he was struck on the way out
steps.stepSummary: Some say he was struck right as he came out of the קודש הקדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: he was struck as he was coming out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another version of the punishment. In this version he was struck right away, not days later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two versions disagree about the timing and manner of his death. Both agree that he was punished from Heaven. The proof for this version comes in the next step.

phrases.english: And some say: as he came out, he was struck,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the punishment told in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He was struck immediately as he left the קודש הקדשים.

steps.title: An angel struck him and left a calf's footprint
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא taught that a sound was heard in the עזרה when an angel struck him. The כהנים found a calf's hoof mark between his shoulders, which matches a פסוק in יחזקאל about angels' feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חייא taught: a kind of sound was heard in the courtyard, because an angel came and struck him on his face. His fellow כהנים came in and found something like a calf's hoof print between his shoulders. As it says: 'Their feet were straight feet, and the soles of their feet were like the sole of a calf's foot.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא of רבי חייא to support the second version. An angel struck him the moment he came out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The calf's hoof print proves an angel did it. The פסוק in יחזקאל describes angels as having feet like a calf's. So the mark on his body is the signature of an angel.

keyTerms.meaning: the sole of a calf's foot

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions agree that the צדוקי כהן גדול was punished from Heaven for lighting the קטורת outside. That is why the elders made the כהן גדול swear an oath.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Chiyya taught:
a kind of sound was heard in the courtyard
because an angel came and struck him on his face.
And his fellow priests came in

phrases.aramaic: וּמָצְאוּ כְּכַף רֶגֶל עֵגֶל בֵּין כְּתֵפָיו,
phrases.english: and found something like a calf's hoof print between his shoulders,
as it is said: 'And their feet were straight feet,'
'and the soles of their feet were like the sole of a calf's foot.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the 'some say' version from Step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That he was struck as soon as he came out
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי חייא, together with the פסוק in יחזקאל 1:7

steps.title: רב corrects a name with a hand signal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's line about רבי זכריה בן קבוטל. When רב חנן בר רבא taught it as 'קפוטל', רב signaled with his hand that it should be 'קבוטל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'רבי זכריה בן קבוטל said...' רב חנן בר רבא taught it to חייא בר רב in front of רב as 'רבי זכריה בן קפוטל said,' and רב showed him with his hand: 'קבוטל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new piece of the משנה, about רבי זכריה בן קבוטל. It tells a story about how his name should be pronounced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב corrected the 'פ' to a 'ב' by gesturing instead of speaking. This unusual detail sets up the next question: why didn't he just say it?

keyTerms.meaning: etc. (the quote continues in the משנה)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זְכַרְיָה בֶּן קְבוּטָל וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Zechariah ben Kevutal said, etc.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנֵי לֵיהּ רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא
phrases.english: Rav Chanan bar Rava taught it
to Chiyya bar Rav in front of Rav
as 'Rabbi Zechariah ben Kefutal said,'
and Rav signaled to him with his hand: 'Kevutal.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זְכַרְיָה בֶּן קְבוּטָל וְכוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The correct name is קבוטל, with a ב.

steps.title: Why didn't רב just say it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב used a hand signal instead of simply saying the correct name.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him just say it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question about the story. Why would רב gesture instead of speaking?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Speaking would have been the normal way to correct someone. The question assumes something must have stopped רב from talking.

phrases.english: Let him just say it to him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the detail in Step 13 that רב gestured.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב corrected the name by gesture rather than speech

steps.title: רב was in the middle of שמע
steps.stepSummary: רב was reciting קריאת שמע and could not stop to speak.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was reciting קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב could not talk because he was in the middle of קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One may not interrupt קריאת שמע with speech. So רב used his hand to correct the mistake without breaking his recitation.

phrases.english: He was reciting the Shema.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב could not speak because he was in the middle of קריאת שמע.

steps.title: But gesturing during שמע is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. רבי יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא said that during שמע one may not wink, signal with the lips, or point with the fingers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is something like this allowed? Didn't רבי יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא say: one who reads שמע should not hint with his eyes, should not signal with his lips, and should not point with his fingers?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer. If gesturing during שמע is forbidden, how could רב do it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 15 assumed that a gesture is fine while speech is not. רבי יצחק's teaching says gestures are also forbidden during שמע. So רב's hand signal seems to break the rule.

phrases.english: And is something like this permitted?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָּא:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta say:

phrases.aramaic: הַקּוֹרֵא אֶת שְׁמַע לֹא יִרְמוֹז בְּעֵינָיו,
phrases.english: one who reads the Shema should not hint with his eyes,
and should not signal with his lips,
and should not point with his fingers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב gestured while reciting שמע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Gestures are forbidden during שמע, so רב could not have gestured in the middle of it.

steps.title: A ברייתא makes the ban even stronger
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר חסמא teaches that one who gestures during שמע is described by the פסוק 'ולא אותי קראת יעקב'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ברייתא teaches that רבי אלעזר חסמא says: one who reads שמע and hints with his eyes, signals with his lips, or points with his finger, about him the פסוק says: 'And you did not call to Me, יעקב.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a ברייתא that backs up the challenge. It shows how serious it is to gesture during שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gesturing during שמע treats it as if it were not really being said to ה׳. That is the point of 'you did not call to Me.' This makes the question on רב even sharper.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you did not call to Me, יעקב' (ישעיה 43:22)

phrases.english: And it was taught: Rabbi Elazar Chisma says:
one who reads the Shema and hints with his eyes,
and signals with his lips, and points with his finger —
about him the verse says:
'And you did not call to Me, Yaakov!'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge of Step 16 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That gesturing during שמע is forbidden and very serious
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי אלעזר חסמא, using ישעיה 43:22

steps.title: First paragraph versus second paragraph
steps.stepSummary: The ban on gesturing applies to the first פרק of שמע. רב gestured during the second פרק, where it is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one is in the first paragraph, and that one is in the second paragraph.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge. It splits שמע into two parts with different rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פרק (accepting ה׳'s kingship) needs full focus, so even gestures are forbidden there. In the second פרק, a gesture for an important need, like correcting a teaching, is allowed. רב was in the second פרק, so his signal was fine.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult (introduces a resolution)

steps.whatToRemember: Gesturing during the first פרק of שמע is forbidden. In the second פרק, a gesture for a real need is allowed. That is how רב could signal 'קבוטל' while saying שמע.
steps.confusionAlert: 'פרק' here does not mean a chapter of the גמרא. It means a paragraph of קריאת שמע: the first is שמע/ואהבת, and the second is והיה אם שמוע.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is in the first paragraph,
that one is in the second paragraph.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּפֶרֶק רִאשׁוֹן, הָא בְּפֶרֶק שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Steps 16 and 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): different rules for different parts of שמע
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any gesture at any point in שמע is forbidden, so רב's signal is a problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban applies only to the first פרק. רב gestured during the second פרק, where it is allowed.

steps.title: One may interrupt שמע but not תפלה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'ודברת בם' to mean that one may interrupt during שמע, but not during תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'And you shall speak of them.' In them (שמע) you may interrupt, but not in תפלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about interrupting. It fits the story about רב, who gestured during שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בם' ('in them') means words of Torah like שמע. That is where some interruption is allowed. תפלה is standing before the King, so it may not be interrupted at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught (this opens a ברייתא)
'And you shall speak of them' (דברים ו:ז)

steps.confusionAlert: 'בם ולא בתפלה' does not mean you say שמע and not תפלה. It is about interrupting: you may interrupt in שמע, but not in תפלה.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"And you shall speak of them"
In them (you may interrupt), but not in prayer.
phrases.notes: שמע may be interrupted. The עמידה may not.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״וְדִבַּרְתָּ בָּם״, בָּם — וְלֹא בִּתְפִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the discussion of רב gesturing during שמע. It adds a source about interrupting שמע compared with תפלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may interrupt during שמע, but not during תפלה.

steps.title: Interrupt only for Torah matters
steps.stepSummary: A second reading of 'ודברת בם': you may speak words of Torah during שמע, but not other things.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And you shall speak of them': about them you have permission to speak, but not about other matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second reading of the same words. This time it limits what kind of interruption is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reading compared שמע with תפלה. This reading looks at the content of the speech. Torah talk is allowed, but everyday talk is not.

phrases.english: "And you shall speak of them"
Of them you have permission to speak,
but not of other matters.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וְדִבַּרְתָּ בָּם״, בָּם יֵשׁ לְךָ רְשׁוּת לְדַבֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second reading of the same פסוק, which limits interruptions to Torah topics.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During שמע one may speak about Torah, but not about other matters.

steps.title: Make Torah fixed, not casual
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא reads 'ודברת בם' to mean that Torah must be a fixed, permanent part of life.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא says: 'And you shall speak of them' means: make them fixed, and do not make them casual.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אחא gives a third reading of the same words. It is about how a person should treat Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'ודברת בם' is not about interruptions. It is a command to make Torah the main thing in life, not a side activity.

phrases.english: Rabbi Acha says:
"And you shall speak of them"
make them permanent
and do not make them temporary.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַחָא אוֹמֵר: ״וְדִבַּרְתָּ בָּם״, עֲשֵׂה אוֹתָן קֶבַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another reading of the same פסוק, about the general attitude toward Torah.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah must be treated as fixed and permanent, not casual.

steps.title: Idle chatter breaks a positive commandment
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that idle chatter breaks the מצות עשה of 'ודברת בם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: One who chats about everyday things breaks a positive commandment, as it says 'And you shall speak of them': of them, and not of other matters.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא uses the same פסוק to make a halachic point about idle talk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He takes 'בם ולא בדברים אחרים' as a real command. Talking about pointless things goes against the מצוה to speak words of Torah.

phrases.english: Rava said:
One who engages in idle chatter
violates a positive commandment,
as it says: "And you shall speak of them"
of them, and not of other matters.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הַשָּׂח שִׂיחַת חוּלִּין — עוֹבֵר בַּעֲשֵׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the reading from step 20 and applies it to idle talk in general.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Idle chatter breaks a מצות עשה.

steps.title: Idle chatter also breaks a negative commandment
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב says idle chatter breaks a לאו, based on a פסוק in קהלת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: One breaks a negative commandment, as it says: 'All matters are wearisome; a man may not speak.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא goes further than רבא and calls idle talk a לאו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'לא יוכל איש לדבר' ('a man cannot speak') as a ban: a man may not speak about empty things. A לאו is a stronger kind of prohibition than an עשה.

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
He violates a negative commandment,
as it says: "All matters are wearisome;
a man may not speak."
phrases.notes: From קהלת א:ח, read here as a rule not to speak.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר: עוֹבֵר בְּלָאו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with רבא, or adds to him: idle talk is a לאו, not only an עשה.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three readings of 'ודברת בם': you may interrupt שמע but not תפלה; you may interrupt only for Torah; Torah must be קבע. Idle talk is an עשה according to רבא and a לאו according to רב אחא בר יעקב.

steps.title: Keeping the כהן גדול awake all night
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: if the כהן גדול starts to doze, the young כהנים snap their fingers and keep him busy until it is time for the morning שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he wanted to doze, the young priests would snap the צרדא finger in front of him and say to him: 'My master, כהן גדול! Stand up and cool yourself once on the floor.' They kept him busy until the time for slaughtering came.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes how the כהנים kept the כהן גדול awake on the night of יום הכיפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול must stay awake so that he does not become טמא through a קרי. The snapping, the reminders, and the walking on the cold floor were all ways to fight sleep. This went on until the morning קרבן תמיד.

keyTerms.meaning: The צרדא finger (explained in the גמרא)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how serious the preparations for the עבודה of יום הכיפורים were.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
If he sought to doze,
the young priests would strike before him
with the tzerada finger (a snap),
and say to him: My master, High Priest!
Stand and cool yourself once on the floor.
And they would keep him occupied
until the time of slaughtering arrived.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It moves from the discussion of שמע back to the night before יום הכיפורים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול is kept awake by snapping, reminders, and activity until the morning שחיטה.

steps.title: Which finger is the צרדא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'צרדא' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is 'צרדא'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking about an unclear word in the משנה. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'צרדא' is not a common word, so the גמרא asks for a definition of the term.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is tzerada?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word in the משנה.

steps.title: The צרדא is the thumb's partner, the middle finger
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that צרדא means 'the partner of that one', that is, the finger paired with the thumb.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: 'The צרה (rival or partner) of this one.' Which one is 'this one'? The thumb.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers by splitting the word into two parts: צרה + דא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'צרתה דדא' means 'the rival of that one', and 'that one' is the thumb. So the צרדא is the middle finger, which presses against the thumb to make a snap.

keyTerms.meaning: Its rival / partner of that one

steps.confusionAlert: The thumb is not the צרדא. The thumb is 'דא' ('that one'). The צרדא is the finger that works against it, the middle finger.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
The rival of that one;
which is that one? The thumb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the word.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: צרדא is the finger paired against the thumb, the middle finger.

steps.title: רב הונא demonstrates how loud the snap is
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא snapped his fingers, and the sound was heard throughout the whole בית מדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא demonstrated it, and the sound went through all of רב's study hall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the topic with a demonstration of how loud this snap is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows that a snap with the middle finger really is loud enough to wake someone. That explains why the משנה chose this method.

phrases.english: Rav Huna demonstrated,
and the sound traveled throughout the entire study hall of Rav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows in practice how effective the finger from step 26 is.
steps.raayaObject: That the צרדא snap is loud enough to keep the כהן גדול awake.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב הונא's demonstration, which filled the בית מדרש with sound.
steps.whatToRemember: The צרדא is the middle finger snapped against the thumb. It makes a very loud sound, used to keep the כהן גדול awake.

steps.title: רב יצחק reads the משנה's phrase as 'introduce something new'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'הפג אחת על הרצפה', and רב יצחק says they should be read as 'על חדת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And they say to him: My master, כהן גדול, cool yourself off once on the floor.' רב יצחק said: it means 'bring in something new'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה. Then רב יצחק gives a new reading of the words 'הפג אחת'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The simple reading is 'cool yourself off once on the cold floor' to shake off sleepiness. רב יצחק reads the letters a little differently, as 'על חדת', which means 'bring in something new'. On his reading, the young כהנים wanted the כהן גדול to do a new activity that would wake him up.

keyTerms.meaning: My master, the כהן גדול (a respectful way to address him)
Floor (the cold floor, used to shake off sleepiness)

phrases.english: And they say to him: My master, High Priest
chill yourself once on the floor, etc.
Rav Yitzchak said: introduce something new.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next phrase of the same משנה about keeping the כהן גדול awake.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's 'הפג אחת' is read as 'על חדת', a request to do something new.

steps.title: What is the new thing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what new activity they asked the כהן גדול to do.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short clarifying question about רב יצחק's reading. It is setting up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Introduce something new' is vague. The גמרא wants to know exactly what activity the כהנים asked for.

phrases.english: What is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the details behind רב יצחק's reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What specific new activity did they request from the כהן גדול?

steps.title: They asked him to demonstrate the special bow
steps.stepSummary: They told the כהן גדול to show them how to perform קידה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say to him: Show us the קידה (the special bow).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the new thing was a demonstration of קידה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קידה was a hard kind of bowing, and the כהן גדול was skilled at it. Doing a physical exercise like this would get his body moving and help keep him awake.

keyTerms.meaning: A difficult kind of formal bowing

phrases.english: They say to him: Demonstrate the ceremonial bowing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The new activity was showing them how to perform קידה.

steps.title: They kept him busy only with singing, not with instruments
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's 'ומעסיקין אותו', and a ברייתא explains that they kept him busy only with their mouths, not with a נבל or a כינור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And they keep him busy until the time of the שחיטה arrives.' A ברייתא taught: They did not keep him busy with a harp or a lyre, only with their mouths.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה. Then it brings a ברייתא that explains how they kept the כהן גדול busy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said 'they kept him busy'. The ברייתא adds that this was done by singing out loud and never with musical instruments. Playing instruments is not allowed on יום טוב, and יום כיפור has that same status.

phrases.english: And they would engage him
until the time of slaughtering arrives, etc.
It was taught: They would not occupy him
not with a harp and not with a lyre,
but rather with the mouth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה's next phrase after finishing with קידה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: They kept the כהן גדול busy only by singing, never with instruments.

steps.title: What did they sing?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what words they sang to the כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what would they say?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks which words they sang. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now know they sang to him. The question is whether the words had a special meaning for him.

phrases.english: And what would they say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the content of the singing mentioned in step 31.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which words did they sing to the כהן גדול?

steps.title: They sang 'Unless ה׳ builds the house'
steps.stepSummary: They sang the פסוק from תהלים: 'אם ה׳ לא יבנה בית, שוא עמלו בוניו בו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Unless ה׳ builds the house, its builders work on it for nothing.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that they sang a פסוק from תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words were chosen on purpose. They reminded the כהן גדול that his עבודה must be done לשם שמים. Without that, all his effort would be wasted.

phrases.english: "Unless the Lord builds the house,
its builders labor in vain on it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They sang תהלים קכז:א, reminding him that his service must be לשם שמים.

steps.title: Jerusalem's leading men stayed awake all night
steps.stepSummary: The prominent men of ירושלים stayed up all night so that the כהן גדול would hear noise and not fall asleep.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some of the prominent men of ירושלים would not sleep the whole night. This was so the כהן גדול would hear the sound of voices and sleep would not overtake him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds that some of the leading men of ירושלים also helped keep the כהן גדול awake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A completely silent city makes it easy to fall asleep. By staying awake and learning, these men kept a steady sound of voices that helped the כהן גדול stay alert.

keyTerms.meaning: The prominent, respected men of ירושלים
The sound of noise or voices

phrases.english: Some of the prominent men of Jerusalem
would not sleep the entire night,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּשְׁמַע כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל קוֹל הֲבָרָה
phrases.english: so that the High Priest would hear the sound of noise
and sleep would not overcome him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיַּקִּירֵי יְרוּשָׁלַיִם לֹא הָיוּ יְשֵׁנִין כׇּל הַלַּיְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds one more way the כהן גדול was kept awake.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Jerusalem's leading men stayed awake all night so the כהן גדול would not fall asleep.

steps.title: אבא שאול: places outside the מקדש copied this, but it led to sin
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול says that people outside ירושלים also stayed up all night as a זכר למקדש, but it led them to sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: אבא שאול said, even in the outlying areas they would do this, as a remembrance of the מקדש. But the result was that they would sin.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא brings אבא שאול's report that the custom spread beyond ירושלים and had a bad result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ירושלים, staying awake had a real purpose: helping the כהן גדול. Elsewhere it was done only as a זכר למקדש, with nothing serious to fill the night. Men and women passed the time together, and this led to sin.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught: Abba Shaul said:
Even in the outlying areas they would do so
in remembrance of the Temple,
but they would sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אַבָּא שָׁאוּל אָמַר: אַף בִּגְבוּלִין הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the Jerusalem custom to other places and notes the harm it caused there.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Outside the מקדש, staying awake on יום כיפור night as a זכר למקדש led to sin.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a good custom taken out of its proper setting can cause harm.

steps.title: אביי: אבא שאול was referring to נהרדעא
steps.stepSummary: אביי (some say רב נחמן בר יצחק) explains that אבא שאול's statement is about נהרדעא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said, and some say it was רב נחמן בר יצחק: Interpret it as referring to נהרדעא.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא tells us which place אבא שאול was talking about. This sets up the story that proves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא שאול spoke in general terms about 'outlying areas'. אביי names the specific place where this sin actually happened: נהרדעא.

keyTerms.meaning: Interpret it as, apply it to
נהרדעא, a major Jewish city in בבל

phrases.english: Abaye said,
and some say Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Interpret it as referring to Nehardea.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the place behind אבא שאול's general statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבא שאול's statement refers to נהרדעא.

steps.title: אליהו tells רב יהודה about the sin in נהרדעא
steps.stepSummary: אליהו told רב יהודה, the brother of רב סלא חסידא, that משיח has not come because of the sins committed in נהרדעא on יום כיפור.
steps.simpleTranslation: As אליהו said to רב יהודה, the brother of רב סלא the pious: You have all asked, 'Why does משיח not come?' But today is יום כיפור, and several unmarried girls were violated in נהרדעא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story with אליהו as proof that the sin happened in נהרדעא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אליהו answers the question of why משיח is delayed. He points to the immorality in נהרדעא on the night of יום כיפור. This confirms אביי's claim that נהרדעא is the place אבא שאול was describing.

phrases.english: As Elijah said

phrases.aramaic: לְרַב יְהוּדָה אֲחוּהּ דְּרַב סַלָּא חֲסִידָא,
phrases.english: to Rav Yehuda, brother of Rav Salla the Pious:
You say: "Why does the Messiah not come?"
But today is Yom Kippur,
and several virgins were violated in Nehardea.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ אֵלִיָּהוּ לְרַב יְהוּדָה אֲחוּהּ דְּרַב סַלָּא חֲסִידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves אביי's identification of נהרדעא.
steps.raayaObject: That אבא שאול's statement refers to נהרדעא
steps.raayaSupportSource: אליהו's words to רב יהודה about the sins in נהרדעא on יום כיפור

steps.title: רב יהודה asks what ה׳ said
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה asks אליהו what הקדוש ברוך הוא said about these sins, and אליהו begins to answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said to him: What did הקדוש ברוך הוא say? אליהו said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה asks how ה׳ reacted, and אליהו begins his reply. The answer itself continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה wants to know whether ה׳ judges these sinners harshly or finds a way to defend them. The step ends right as אליהו starts to answer.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַאי אָמַר?
phrases.english: He said to him: What did the Holy One, Blessed be He, say?
He said to him:
phrases.notes: The answer continues on the next amud

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַאי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the conversation between אליהו and רב יהודה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What did ה׳ say about the sins committed in נהרדעא?
